description: One flawless sphere, off-white with a lilac sheen. Nobody will say which water it was brought up out of.
lore: Gold buys goods. A pearl is what you put on the table when the thing you want is not for sale, and at a hundred and ten it is well clear of the price of anything a person actually needs.

A man set one down in front of [[characters/ef25b1f0|Bettany]] and asked her to leave a name out of [[lore/the_chronicle|the Chronicle]]. Not his own. She did not take it and she did not argue with him. She wrote the offer down instead — the date, the sphere, the lilac in it, what it would have fetched, and the fact that a man had believed the book was the sort of thing that could be bought, which she noted was the more interesting half of the evening. She left his name out. That part he did get.
gm_notes: Bettany's incorruptibility played as comedy, with a standing question underneath: whose name, and why is it worth a hundred and ten gold to somebody else that it stay out. The pearl is still in his coat.
